rationale: 3 blocking findings: _detect_terminal_truncation never resets _last_finish_reason/_last_truncated on a non-truncated match, so a truncated intermediate/subagent turn can leak into a later successful final answer, matching the acceptance lens's partial spec item (critical, CR-002); the new is_finish_reason_truncated check is gated behind is_valid_ai_message, so non-streaming terminal messages with non-empty content skip truncation detection entirely (major, CR-004); and a commit removed, with no stated rationale in the commit message or any intervening ticket commit, the threading.Lock that an earlier review round (commit 8ace3e510) had added specifically to guard this same _last_finish_reason/_last_truncated state (major, downgraded from critical, CR-001). CR-001 was independently re-verified rather than taken at face value: no code path currently invokes the same LangGraphAgent instance concurrently - the sub-workflow WorkflowPool's acquire()/release() checkout (workflow_pool.py) is mutually exclusive under a lock, held for the full synchronous duration of the child execution; the only genuinely concurrent dispatch mechanism, the Send-based parallel-iteration fan-out in WorkflowExecutor.continue_iteration (workflow.py), always builds a fresh, unshared LangGraphAgent per parallel branch because those AgentNodes are constructed via init_agent_node with no assistant kwarg, so AgentNode.assistant stays None and generate_execution_context's `self.assistant or self.init_assistant(...)` never caches an instance to share; and the one path that does persist a single shared instance across turns, SupervisorWorkflowExecutor.build_workflow, routes strictly one next speaker at a time (add_conditional_edges with a single-key map, no Send, no fan-out) - so persistence and concurrency never combine on the same instance today. This is therefore not a live, exploitable bug, but the removal deletes the only guard against a future change (e.g. caching an assistant onto a node that also participates in a Send fan-out) silently reintroducing the exact cross-contamination class the lock was written to catch. 3 findings deferred as genuinely pre-existing and spec-scoped (legacy AssistantAgent.invoke_task never threading truncation signals; the top-level WorkflowExecution/response model never receiving the new fields; and the pre-existing _get_truncation_indicator allow-list not recognizing Vertex AI/Gemini's raw finish-reason enum value 'MAX_TOKENS' - confirmed via installed package source, but that allow-list function is unmodified by this diff and the spec's own provider-coverage criterion scopes testing to OpenAI/LiteLLM, native Claude, and Bedrock only) - see code-review-deferred.md. 2 dismissed as spec-sanctioned noise (tool-call raise-and-fail path not carrying truncated info onto the FAILED TaskResult/state, already covered by the existing agent_token_limit error-code channel). Standards audit ran clean with no coverage gap. Confidence raised to high: aws_bedrock (ChatBedrockConverse's stopReason, confirmed via the botocore bedrock-runtime service model) and azure_openai/LiteLLM-proxied (OpenAI's finish_reason literal type) are both exactly covered by the existing allow-list, closing the only reachability uncertainty that had held confidence to medium.

findings.title: Concurrent-invocation lock removed, with no replacement guard, no stated rationale
findings.problem: A commit titled 'Remove concurrent-invocation lock from LangGraphAgent.invoke_task' deleted the threading.Lock (self._invoke_lock) that an earlier review round (commit 8ace3e510, that round's CR-003) had added around invoke_task specifically to guard the new _last_finish_reason/_last_truncated instance attributes against concurrent access, raising RuntimeError if a second call was in flight. The removal commit's message carries no rationale beyond its subject line, and no intervening ticket commit documents why the guard was no longer needed; no replacement (e.g. moving the state to a per-call-local object or contextvar) was introduced in its place.
findings.impact: Re-verified independently rather than accepted at face value, from primary source rather than the diff alone: no code path in the current codebase invokes the same LangGraphAgent instance's invoke_task concurrently. The one mechanism that reuses a compiled graph (and any embedded LangGraphAgent) across different executions, WorkflowPool.acquire/release (src/codemie/service/workflow_pool.py), checks a graph out exclusively under a lock for the full synchronous duration of one child execution before releasing it back to the pool - reuse across time, never across concurrency. The one mechanism capable of genuinely concurrent execution, WorkflowExecutor.continue_iteration's Send-based parallel-iteration fan-out (src/codemie/workflows/workflow.py), dispatches N concurrent branches to the same target node, but that node's AgentNode is built via init_agent_node with no assistant kwarg, so AgentNode.assistant stays None and generate_execution_context's `self.assistant or self.init_assistant(...)` builds - and never caches - a fresh, unshared LangGraphAgent on every call, including every concurrent branch. The one mechanism that does persist a single shared LangGraphAgent instance across turns, SupervisorWorkflowExecutor.build_workflow (src/codemie/workflows/supervisor_workflow.py:89-122), routes to exactly one next speaker per turn via a single-key conditional edge - no Send, no fan-out - so it is sequential, never concurrent. Persistence and concurrency never combine on the same instance today, so this is not a live, exploitable bug. But the removal deletes the only guard against a future change (e.g. a node built with a persistent assistant= that later also participates in a Send fan-out, or any new caching layer) silently reintroducing the exact cross-contamination class the lock was written to catch - and that class has already occurred once, since the lock existed specifically to fix it.
findings.recommendation: Given no live path currently triggers this, a full RuntimeError-raising lock may be more defensive than the risk warrants - but leaving the invariant completely unenforced is also not free, since it already regressed once. Consider a lighter-weight guard: e.g. a debug-mode assertion/reentrancy check on invoke_task, or a short comment plus a unit test asserting AgentNode never caches a persistent assistant onto a node reachable via Send/continue_iteration, so a future violation fails a test instead of silently corrupting a response.

findings.title: Truncation flag never reset between turns
findings.problem: _detect_terminal_truncation only ever sets _last_finish_reason/_last_truncated when it finds a truncation match; it never resets them to None/False when a terminal message is not truncated, even though it is invoked once per terminal message within a single invoke_task call (once per subagent turn via parse_supervisor_message_type in supervisor flows).
findings.impact: A truncated intermediate or subagent terminal message can leave _last_truncated=True set even after a later, genuinely-complete final terminal message of the same invoke_task call is processed, so a fully successful response can be persisted and returned with a false truncated=True/finish_reason; the spec's own per-turn reset requirement is only partially met (acceptance lens grades this spec item partial), and no test in the diff drives two terminal messages (truncated-then-not) through the same call.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit reset branch in _detect_terminal_truncation (or reset immediately before each terminal-message check) so a non-truncated match clears _last_finish_reason=None/_last_truncated=False, matching the spec's requirement to reset per supervisor turn.

findings.title: Non-streaming truncation detection skipped
findings.problem: In both parse_message_type and parse_supervisor_message_type (lines 146-152 and 180-185), the new is_finish_reason_truncated() check was added only to the elif branch, which never runs when is_valid_ai_message(message) is True - and is_valid_ai_message only checks that message.content is non-empty, regardless of finish_reason. Non-streaming LLM invocations (streaming=False configs exist in this codebase, e.g. llm_factory.py) typically yield a single terminal AIMessage chunk carrying both full content and full response_metadata.
findings.impact: For non-streaming model configurations, a terminal message that is both non-empty and truncated is routed into the content/streaming branch instead of the elif, so _detect_terminal_truncation never runs and the truncation goes completely undetected for that configuration, defeating the new feature's core purpose.
findings.recommendation: Check is_finish_reason_truncated(message) independently of is_valid_ai_message (e.g. call _detect_terminal_truncation before or outside the if/elif content-based branch) so truncation detection isn't gated on the message having empty content.
